udt_union_v0.doc: SEP-40 asset key: a Stellar token, or a ticker symbol.
udt_union_v0.name: Asset

udt_struct_v0.doc: SEP-40 price record: `price` in the oracle's `decimals`, quoted in its `base`.
udt_struct_v0.name: PriceData

tuple_v0.doc: Temporary-storage cache of a fully resolved price read, keyed by our-asset\nAddress \xe2\x86\x92 [`PriceCache`]. Valid only within the ledger it was written in.
tuple_v0.name: PriceCache

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A cached resolved price: the asset's WAD USD price, its source timestamp in seconds,
the freshness verdict, and the ledger the cache was written in. Any repeat read of the
same asset within a tx (an account with several positions in one pool prices the same
underlying over and over; the margin gate touches both a share and its underlying)
skips the source's cross-contract call \xe2\x80\x94 a fresh ~1MB VM instantiation charged against
the tx memory cap. Caching the whole resolved triple (not a raw feed value) covers
every source uniformly \xe2\x80\x94 Sep40, RedStone, and the derived YieldShare, whose base and
wrapper-rate calls are both skipped on a hit. `fresh` is safe to cache: within one
ledger `now` is constant, so the verdict cannot flip. Same-ledger validity bounds the
staleness this can mask to one ledger (~5s), far inside any registered `max_age`.
udt_struct_v0.name: PriceCache

udt_union_v0.doc: How an asset's USD price is sourced.
udt_union_v0.name: PriceSource

tuple_v0.doc: Derived: the base asset's price scaled by the wrapper's share\xe2\x86\x92underlying rate.
tuple_v0.name: YieldShare

udt_struct_v0.doc: A SEP-40 source: which oracle + asset key, the oracle's decimals, freshness bound.
udt_struct_v0.name: Sep40Source

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A XOXNO price-aggregator source: the aggregator contract, the key this asset is quoted under
there, and the freshness bound.

No `decimals`: the aggregator already answers in WAD. Its own `asset_decimals` describes the
asset, not the price.

The aggregator resolves each key from one or more underlying feeds and applies its own
staleness and dual-source-deviation checks; the hub reads the *soft* side of that
(`quote`) and decides for itself what counts as usable, so an asset XOXNO considers
questionable degrades to "no price" instead of reverting every valuation that touches it.
udt_struct_v0.name: XoxnoSource

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A RedStone Adapter source: the network's shared adapter contract, the feed id it
keys this asset's price under ("USDC", "XLM", \xe2\x80\xa6), the deployment's price decimals
(8 on RedStone's Stellar deployments \xe2\x80\x94 the adapter doesn't expose it on-chain, so
it's recorded at registration), and the freshness bound. Adapter timestamps are
always milliseconds; the hub normalizes on read.
udt_struct_v0.name: RedStoneSource

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A yield-share source: a share token whose price is *derived* rather than quoted. `base_asset`
is the underlying (registered in the hub under its own source), `wrapper` the yield wrapper
exposing `assets_per_share_wad()` \xe2\x80\x94 how much underlying one whole share is currently worth.

Exists because a yield-bearing share is not worth its underlying 1:1: the rate grows as
interest accrues, so quoting the share at the underlying's price understates it by exactly the
accrued yield. There is no external oracle for such a share \xe2\x80\x94 the rate is on-chain \xe2\x80\x94 hence a
derived source rather than another feed.
udt_struct_v0.name: YieldShareSource

function_v0.doc: Every registered asset, in registration order (lets consumers enumerate the hub).
function_v0.name: assets

function_v0.doc: Replace the contract's wasm (admin-gated). Address and storage are kept.
function_v0.name: upgrade

function_v0.doc: Transfer the admin role to `new_admin` (current admin only). Hands the hub over to the\ngovernance timelock; the price-source routing (`set_sep40_source` /\n`set_redstone_feed_source`) moves with the role.
function_v0.name: set_admin

function_v0.doc: Storage/schema version, bumped by a post-`upgrade` migration when the layout changes.
function_v0.name: get_version

cases.doc: The base price multiplied by the live share rate does not fit the hub's price type.
cases.name: YieldSharePriceOverflow

cases.doc: A RedStone `U256` price does not fit the hub's signed `i128` price representation.
cases.name: RedStonePriceOutOfRange

cases.doc: Normalizing a quoted price to WAD does not fit `i128`.
cases.name: PriceScaleOverflow

function_v0.doc:
Unregister `asset`'s price source (admin only): it prices as `(0, 0, false)` again,
exactly like an asset that was never routed. The escape hatch for a wedged feed \xe2\x80\x94 a
yield wrapper whose upstream broke, a decommissioned oracle \xe2\x80\x94 so it can be neutralised
without inventing a fake quoted price. Re-registering via `set_*_source` restores it.
function_v0.name: remove_source

function_v0.doc: Route `asset` to a SEP-40 oracle (Reflector / RedStone SEP-40), keyed by\n`sep40_asset` (admin only). Caches the oracle's `decimals()`.
function_v0.name: set_sep40_source

function_v0.doc:
Route `asset` to XOXNO's price aggregator under `key` (admin only).

Probes with the fail-closed `price` rather than the soft `quote` the hub reads at runtime:
registration is the one moment we *want* a hard failure. A key the aggregator cannot
resolve would otherwise register cleanly and price the asset `(0, 0, false)` forever, which
downstream reads as "stale oracle" and traps every valuation touching it \xe2\x80\x94 far from the
call that actually got it wrong.
function_v0.name: set_xoxno_source

function_v0.doc:
USD price of `asset` in WAD (1e18), the source timestamp, and a freshness flag.
Returns `(0, 0, false)` when no source is registered, a quoted source has no price,
or a source read fails. Every arm degrades rather than trapping: this hub sits inside
every margin, liquidation and settlement flow, and consumers cannot guard a panic in a
dependency \xe2\x80\x94 one wedged source would freeze all of them for every account holding the
asset (S2-M-04). "No price" is the one verdict consumers already handle safely.
function_v0.name: get_price_usd_wad

function_v0.doc:
Route `asset` to a feed on the RedStone Adapter (admin only). `feed_id` is the
adapter's key for the asset ("USDC", "XLM", "BENJI", \xe2\x80\xa6); `decimals` is the
deployment's price scale \xe2\x80\x94 8 on RedStone's Stellar deployments (the adapter
doesn't expose it on-chain). Probes the adapter once so a wrong adapter address
or feed id fails here instead of silently pricing as `(0, 0, false)`.
function_v0.name: set_redstone_source

function_v0.doc:
Route a yield-wrapper `share` to its underlying's price scaled by the wrapper's live
share\xe2\x86\x92underlying rate (admin only). `base_asset` must already have a quoted source; a
derived base is rejected so sources cannot nest.

The three arguments must describe **one** wrapper: `share` and `base_asset` are checked
against the wrapper's own `share_token()` and `underlying()`, so the triple cannot be
assembled from parts of two.

Probing the rate is not enough on its own \xe2\x80\x94 it passes for any contract exposing
`assets_per_share_wad() > 0`, which is every other wrapper in the deployment. Registration
happens in a loop over reserves and tenors, so a transposed pair is a live risk, and it
produces a *well-formed* price: the share ends up quoted at some other asset's price times
this wrapper's rate. Nothing downstream can tell \xe2\x80\x94 the error is a constant factor, so it
reads as a plausible number and mis-values margin by the ratio of the two assets until an
off-chain reconciliation catches it.

Also probes the base price
function_v0.name: set_yield_share_source

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Adapter price record. `price` is in the deployment's fixed decimals (8 on
RedStone's Stellar deployments). Both timestamps are **milliseconds**:
`package_timestamp` is when the oracle nodes signed the data (the price's true
age), `write_timestamp` when an updater pushed it on-chain.
udt_struct_v0.name: RedStonePriceData

udt_struct_v0.doc:
One swap hop through a specific pool.

`amount_out` is ignored by the aggregator \xe2\x80\x94 it derives the honorable output from live reserves \xe2\x80\x94
so a payload built on-chain can leave it at `0`.
udt_struct_v0.name: SwapHop

udt_struct_v0.doc: One sub-route: a sequence of hops taking `split_ppm` (parts-per-million) of the total input.
udt_struct_v0.name: SwapPath

udt_union_v0.doc: A DEX the aggregator can route a hop through. Mirrors the Router's own `SwapVenue`.
udt_union_v0.name: SwapVenue

udt_struct_v0.doc:
The full route. `total_min_out` is the only slippage bound the aggregator itself enforces.

Field names and types mirror the Router's ABI **exactly** \xe2\x80\x94 the payload crosses the boundary as
XDR ([`soroban_sdk::xdr::ToXdr`]), so a renamed or reordered field does not fail to compile, it
fails to decode on the other side.
udt_struct_v0.name: StrategyPayload

udt_union_v0.doc:
What a price is keyed by in XOXNO's aggregator: a token address, or a symbolic reference for a
quote that has no token of its own (an index, a synthetic pair).

Mirrors `common::types::composable_oracle::PriceKey`.
udt_union_v0.name: PriceKey

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A XOXNO market coordinate: the same underlying can be listed as several isolated markets
(separate indexes, cash, bad debt), so a market is `(hub_id, asset)`, not just `asset`.
Field names/types mirror XOXNO's `common::types::HubAssetKey` exactly (a two-field struct
XOXNO encodes as an XDR map keyed by field name), so it decodes on both the argument and the
map-key side.
udt_struct_v0.name: HubAssetKey

udt_struct_v0.doc:
The aggregator's soft read: a resolved price plus why it might not be usable. Mirrors
`common::types::oracle::PriceStatus`.

`final_wad` is already WAD-scaled USD, so nothing needs re-scaling on our side \xe2\x80\x94
`asset_decimals` on the fail-closed `PriceFeedRaw` describes the *asset*, not the price.

The three flags are the reason this, and not `price`, is what the hub calls:

* `valid` \xe2\x80\x94 the aggregator could resolve anything at all. `false` means no usable price.
* `stale` \xe2\x80\x94 the newest observation is older than the asset's configured bound.
* `deviation` \xe2\x80\x94 two independent sources disagree beyond the configured tolerance. Not an
error on XOXNO's side, but for a margin engine it is exactly the case where a price should
not be trusted.
udt_struct_v0.name: PriceStatus

udt_enum_v0.doc:
Leverage/position mode for `multiply`. A `u32`-discriminant enum mirroring XOXNO's
`common::types::PositionMode` exactly (values must match, or the call decodes to the wrong mode).
`Multiply` allows the same asset across different hubs (passthrough, no swap); `Long`/`Short`
require distinct assets and a real swap route.
udt_enum_v0.name: PositionMode

udt_struct_v0.doc:
The aggregator's fail-closed read: it reverts rather than hand back a price it considers
stale, deviating or unresolvable. Mirrors `common::types::oracle::PriceFeedRaw`.

`price_wad` is USD in WAD; `asset_decimals` describes the *asset*, not the price, so nothing
here needs re-scaling.
udt_struct_v0.name: PriceFeedRaw

udt_struct_v0.doc: A market's supply and borrow indexes, RAY-scaled (1e27). Mirrors XOXNO's\n`common::types::MarketIndexRaw`.
udt_struct_v0.name: MarketIndexRaw
